page: Microsoft Azure E8s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv3 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz, offering 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance features 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It includes 131 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates that the E8s_v3 exhibits moderate memory performance and weaker raw compute capabilities. Its stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 25 percent, as do its Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores. However, memory bandwidth tests for both cached small blocks and uncached large blocks show average performance in the middle 50 percent tier. Passmark CPU and memory scores also align with average tier expectations, alongside average performance in Redis SET operations and database operations.

The primary tradeoff of the E8s_v3 is its modest CPU compute speed relative to its generous memory allocation. While compute-intensive tasks like LLM text generation on medium models perform poorly, the instance is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high CPU throughput. Appropriate workloads include relational databases, caching layers like Redis, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring a larger memory footprint.
description: Microsoft Azure E8s_v3 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine from the ESv3 family, powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. It features 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 64.0 GB of system memory, and a 131 GB local SSD. The instance delivers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, making it suitable for memory-bound applications. Benchmark results show average performance in memory bandwidth, Passmark database operations, and Redis SET operations, though raw CPU compute and single-core performance fall into the lower 25 percent tier. This hardware profile presents a tradeoff of high memory capacity against moderate processing power. It is best suited for database hosting, caching layers, and memory-intensive enterprise workloads.
